dxerr9.lib — Microsoft DirectX error-reporting library, as linked into game.dat
=============================================================================

dxerr9.lib
  sha256  81204fd2c9e1be4abc63772e694f9d4c82b057611b4b64e81c2c58910fdcbe0a
  size    4,360,028 bytes
  dated   2005-07-22
  from    DirectX 9.0c SDK (August 2005), Lib/x86/DxErr9.lib, inside
          dxsdk_aug2005.exe (md5 053c7a32ce3d7982eb1191863d4e2ddb,
          https://archive.org/details/dxsdk_aug2005)

Why this SDK
------------
game.dat imports d3dx9_27.dll, the D3DX runtime of the August 2005 SDK.
The Summer 2003 archive in vendor/dxerr9/ (kept for BFME 1) places only one
of its fourteen bodies uniquely here; this one places all eighteen of its
code COMDATs.

Region
------
RVA 0x0062AFE0-0x00654778 (169,880 bytes), with import thunks on both sides;
comsupp's first row follows at 0x006547C0. The single member
obj\i386\dxerr9.obj supplies every body, in archive order.

Placement
---------
Each COMDAT was compared against .text over its full length with relocation
sites masked. Ten place once. The other eight are four A/W pairs whose masked
bytes are identical (DXGetErrorDescription9, StringCchCopy, StringCchPrintf,
StringCchLength); each pair has exactly two hits for two archive instances.
Archive order puts A first, and two retail facts confirm it: every one of the
28 internal calls lands on the placement of the callee it names, and all 626
string pointers in each DXGetErrorDescription9 body point at narrow strings
for A and wide strings for W.

Rows sourced here carry `vendored=dxerr9-aug2005` and name the archive member
their bytes come from; ./build.sh extracts that member and byte-compares it
against retail like any other row.
